title: Prompt contract manifest and performance profile publishing spec
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define a machine- and human-readable contract that teams must publish when onboarding a pinned model version. The contract covers three orthogonal areas: 1) prompt/IO schema and normalization rules, 2) stable parameter/flag aliases and behavior expectations, and 3) a published performance profile (latency, throughput, resource usage) tied to a canonical workload distribution. This ticket produces the contract manifest spec (manifest.json schema v1.0), a lightweight validation tool, and a required checklist for model onboarding engineers and PMs. The contract is intended to be enforced by CI gates in the onboarding pipeline and surfaced in Console onboarding flows.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON manifest schema (contract_schema: "1.0") that includes: model_identifier, pinned_version, prompt_schema reference, parameter_alias_map, deterministic_fields_list, tolerated_semantic_shift thresholds, and performance_profile metadata.

A canonical prompt normalization document that specifies tokenization expectations, whitespace/Unicode normalization, canonical separators for structured outputs (e.g., JSON-lines vs. JSON), and required stable keys for tool-calling outputs.
Parameter alias mapping rules that define supported synonyms (e.g., temperature -> temp) and which parameter changes are allowed without breaking the contract.

Performance profile format with sample input-length distribution, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory/GPU footprint, and quantization profile tags. Profiles must include measurement methodology and environment labels (hardware, driver, runtime).

A validation CLI that checks a candidate manifest and runs a small battery of regression prompts (provided harness) comparing semantic similarity and output shape invariants against the pinned baseline.
CI gate configuration example that fails onboarding if semantic shift exceeds thresholds or if performance regressions exceed configured deltas for the target release tier.
discussion: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with PM + Research. Agreed scope: focus on pinned versions for hosted and dedicated; Private will consume the same manifest but may add environment-specific overrides.

2025-02-18: Trade-off: strict deterministic guarantees are impossible for some stochastic models. Decided to separate 'shape contracts' (hard) from 'semantic-conservation' metrics (soft thresholds with alerts).
2025-02-21: Design review (Priya Nair): recommended including a stable 'output_key_map' for tool-calling to avoid downstream breakage when model adds keys.
2025-02-25: Engineering review (Liam O'Connor): suggested adding an explicit 'tokenizer_version' field and a hash of vocabulary to detect tokenizer drift. Added to schema.

2025-02-28: Security note (Sofia Alvarez): no sensitive content must be included in published manifests; ensure KMS-protected links for any private artifacts. Marked security_review_required=false for this iteration, but private deployments will require review.
implementation_notes: Manifest layout: top-level fields: contract_schema, model_id, pinned_revision, created_by, uploaded_by, prompt_schema_uri, parameter_alias_map_uri, deterministic_keys, semantic_thresholds, performance_profile_uri, release_tier, compliance_tags.

Prompt schema: JSON Schema that describes expected inputs (field names, types, max lengths) plus normalization rules (NFKC, trim, collapse whitespace). Include canonical examples for structured prompts used in evals.

Parameter alias rules: list of {alias, canonical_name, allowed_range, mutability}. E.g., alias="temp", canonical="temperature", allowed_range=0-2.0, mutability=runtime|fixed. Mutability=runtime means clients may change within allowed_range without violating contract.

Semantic stability check: use multiple eval metrics (embedding cosine, token-level BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs) with a defensible threshold and confidence intervals. Default semantic_thresholds: embedding_cosine_min=0.92, structured_output_match_rate_min=0.98 for canonical prompts in harness.

Performance profile: include environment tags (gpu_family, driver_version), measured p50/p95 for target request size buckets (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024 tokens), tokens_per_second, peak_gpu_mem_mb, and quantization_profile tags (fp16, int8, q4f16).

Storage/publishing: manifests are stored under s3://redwood-model-manifests/{model_id}/{pinned_revision}/manifest.json and referenced in Console UI. Public hosted manifests also mirrored to the models catalog with signed URLs.

Validation tool: shim that pulls manifest, runs 100-sample regression harness using the pinned baseline and the candidate build, and reports semantic and performance deltas. Should exit non-zero when hard shape invariants fail or when semantic thresholds are crossed beyond configured slack.

CI integration: example GitHub Action and internal pipeline step names provided. Gate types: shape-fail (hard), semantic-warning (soft, can block on P0 onboarding), perf-regression (block for release-tier=enterprise).
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest schema validation (positive and negative cases).
Integration test that runs the validation CLI against a known-good pinned manifest and a synthetic regression manifest.
Canary rollout for the validator: enable for 10% of onboarding flows for 2 weeks, collect false positive rates and adjust thresholds.
Manual review checklist for initial 20 onboarded models: PM sign-off on semantic thresholds and performance profile acceptance.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly-strict semantic thresholds will block legitimate model improvements. Mitigation: provide a staged bypass process involving PM/Research review and a documented rollback path.

Risk: Measurement noise in performance profiles across hardware. Mitigation: require environment labels and use normalized baselines; prefer relative deltas with confidence intervals instead of single-sample comparisons.
Risk: Clients rely on optional fields. Mitigation: clearly mark required vs. optional fields in schema and add Console warnings when optional fields are missing.
